text:
Tampa Bay won this one in the first period. Charle-Edouard D'Astous scored 2:26 in, and Conor Geekie made it 2-0 at 16:30, with Brandon Hagel and Jake Guentzel assisting on both. TBL out-chanced WSH 1.62 to 0.41 in expected goals over those 20 minutes, and the lead held up even after the game tilted the other way.

It did tilt. WSH's lone goal came in the second, when Justin Sourdif tipped one in on a 1% chance, with Jakob Chychrun and Boone Jenner assisting. By the third, Washington was the better side, 1.53 expected goals to 1.13. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 of 21 shots against an expected 2.53 goals, which is 1.53 goals better than average, and that kept the comeback from finishing. Charlie Lindgren was good at the other end (27 saves, 1.11 goals above expected), but Washington never turned its third-period push into a second goal.

Guentzel sealed it at 17:55 of the third with a wrist shot, set up by Nikita Kucherov and John Carlson, making it 3-1. TBL finished with 2.53 to 3.59 in total expected goals against WSH and a 60% share of simulated replays, so the win was earned rather than stolen. Neither team scored on the power play (WSH 0 for 2, TBL 0 for 3), and Washington took 25 penalty minutes to Tampa Bay's 13. Hagel's two assists and six shots on goal showed how much of the offense ran through him.
